answer: According to arXiv 2410.01871, the relationship between the cost of acquiring minority class data and equalized odds in the Fairface case study is that as the percentage of minority class data increases (which represents a greater cost), the equalized odds metric improves, indicating greater compliance. This means that collecting more minority class data leads to a larger and more balanced dataset, which in turn results in better equalized odds performance on well-balanced test data for the models trained on various mixtures of data.
